title: Akhenaten
summary: Akhenaten, born Amenhotep IV, was an Eighteenth Dynasty pharaoh who made the sun disk Aton Egypt's state god and moved the capital from Thebes to a new city, Akhetaten (modern Amarna). The sources date his reign differently, from about 1377-1360 BCE to about 1350-1334 BCE. His successors restored the traditional religion and returned the capital to Thebes.

uncertainty.note: The dates are the span of the reign. EBSCO gives around 1377 to 1360 BCE (astronomical -1376 to -1359); Encyclopedia.com's Ikhnaton entry says he ruled about 1350 to 1334 bce (-1349 to -1333), and its other entry gives c. 1385-1350 B.C. so start and end may be up to 27 and 26 years later than the figures used.

when.display: reigned c. 1377-1360 BCE (EBSCO) or c. 1350-1334 BCE (Encyclopedia.com)

where.historical_name: Akhetaten, the capital Akhenaten founded, in the Egypt of the Eighteenth Dynasty

importance.justification: His state worship of Aton and the new capital at Amarna were a sharp break in Egyptian religion and art.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the dates: opened sources disagree by about 25 years and Encyclopedia.com's two entries differ from each other, so the range is wide. I did not state the monotheism question. Pin is the Amarna site he founded, not a birthplace.
